Messages.Author: TorranceCircle
Messages.Body:
I'm redoing the walls in my kitchen and need some wallpaper

After seeing some posts in another thread, it seems some players have different ideas about what makes a card wallpaper. I've always thought the term meant cards that were so bad they were a detriment to even have in a deck.

What are your top 5 wallpaper cards and why? Also, have you ever made a deck with a card to prove it was not wallpaper? What were the results?

Someone wrote that Wake with Evening's Freshness is wallpaper. I don't think that's completely the case. Perhaps this discussion will help others see ways to possibly use some cards they never would have before.

Messages.Author: CryWolf
Messages.Body:
> TorranceCircle wrote:
> After seeing some posts in another thread, it seems some players have different ideas about what makes a card wallpaper. I've always thought the term meant cards that were so bad they were a detriment to even have in a deck.
>
I've always thought that "wallpaper" meant that the card has been rendered "obsolete" because of a new card does the same thing but more efficiently, or with better side effects, etc.

A "wallpapered" card may have been useful before, but with the introduction of the better card(s), has been rendered useless/sub-optimal.

> What are your top 5 wallpaper cards and why? Also, have you ever made a deck with a card to prove it was not wallpaper? What were the results? Someone wrote that Wake with Evening's Freshness is wallpaper. I don't think that's completely the case. Perhaps this discussion will help others see ways to possibly use some cards they never would have before.
>
I must say Twisting the Knife takes the cake. Pulled Fangs does the same thing (inflict 1 more damage) but it can trigger more easily, is free, is more common, has been around longer, etc. etc. I never bothered to make a deck with it.

I disagree that WWEF is wallpaper. It has its own uses, even if the draw back can be steep. I use WWEF if I expect to react with the same minion more than once between turns, but do not intend to block. I find that a mix of WWEF and OtQV works well for non-dedicated block decks. But of course, YMMV.

Advocate of  Good-looking Deck Posts

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
I would go for the old "clan weakness" card. They are fun to read, often don't exactly do much, are non-trifle master, and aren't too useful even if they are vampires of this clan.

But apart from thoses "historical" cards

1 - Combat shotgun : .44 magnum really put this card to shame I believe. The sawed-off seem pretty bad too, but at least it's cheaper for more or less the same effect.
2 - Bonecraft. Weak effect while being costly in opportunity cost - if you can do a close range strike, maybe you should do aggravated damage instead ?
3 - Immense Size. Press or immortal grapple aren't too much of a problem for vis combat. You may use it to support the vis combat end, but chiroptean marauder will usually work way better.
4 - Excommunication. Very situationnal and not exactly game-changing when it does have a target
5 - Kuta. Banishment has less restriction and will have much more of an effect.

Note that I don't believe that Vissicitude is weak. It's just one of my favorite discipline, and it have along powerfuls and versatils card like Chiroptean marauder some ... dubious card

Messages.Author: echiang
Messages.Body:
> Baaliprimogen wrote:
> 4. Jua Vema (simillar to Skin of Night, only requiers more and does less)
> 5. Art of Love, The (Entrancement anyone?)
>
Jua Vema is hardly wallpaper. In the right deck, you can have rush actions that cannot be blocked by vampires. (Do a rush action, play Daring the Dawn, and during the resulting combat use Jua Vema to convert the Daring the Dawn agg into normal).

Art of Love isn't amazing, but it's a solid and usable card. Someone else already mentioned using it with War Ghouls. Alternatively, you can steal someone's Carlton or War Ghoul and immediately burn them with their innate abilities. You can similarly kill Infernal Servitors with it. Against the Imbued, it's useful to "fake out" the Imbued player by tricking him into burning his React with Conviction (and you then follow-up with a *real* Entrancement to keep the ally for good).

> extrala wrote:
> Crimson Fury -- way too conditional
>
Can be amusing with Reform Body. "For all your efforts, you burn and I stick around."

> Sonja Blue -- building on deck on vampire that is constantly under threat of being hijacked? Jacob, The Glitch -- losing your hand over and over again? Miguel Cordovera -- paying 6 pool to give my predator a vampire to bleed me? Hector Trelane -- giving someone pool when my vampire goes to torpor (or is burned)?
>
I do agree with this list though. Really debilitating disadvantages (why do they predominantly appear on Tremere and !Tremere though?). If Hector Trelane had been made after KMW, he would simply have had Red List which would have made him a bit more playable.

> Non-existant user wrote:
> 3) Day Operation. Daring is plain better.
>
Well, it *used* to be decent in the old days when it prevented *all* block attempts (by vampires *and* allies). Nowadays, it might be *slightly* useful if you have inferior  guys who have ways to reduce the cost of cards (like Masochism?). But yeah, generally it is worse than Daring the Dawn.

> 5) Can we nominate THN combat as a whole?
>
Groaning Corpse is good. Compress is expensive but a pretty good way to burn vampires. Creeping Infection is actually good for a bleed deck. Withering can be quite good in the right deck.

> blackday wrote:
> 4. Betrayer
>
Betrayer is very weak but it has its uses in Uriah Winter decks. I've also seen Pander decks with the Group 4 Pander try and use it (with varying degrees of success).

> nc-italy wrote:
> Consume the Dead
>
Consume the Dead isn't that bad. I've seen Nagaraja put it to good use to recoup the cost of Shambling Hordes or Masquer (Wraith). It's also not that uncommon to see some minion/retainer burned during a typical game.
